### Identification

Once we have specified the hypothetical quantities from our thought experiment, we "identify" them, meaning write them in terms of the observed rather than counterfactual model. It is sufficient to identify the quantity:






$$
\begin{aligned}
E[Y_i^{(a)}]                    &= E \left[ E[Y_i^{(a)} | L_i] \right] \\
                                &= E \left[ E[f_{Y}(U_{Y_i} , L_i, a) | L_i] \right] \\
                                &= E \left[ E[f_{Y}(U_{Y_i} , L_i, a) | L_i , A_i] \right] \\
                                &= E \left[ E[f_{Y}(U_{Y_i} , L_i, a) | L_i , A_i = a] \right] \\
                                &= E \left[ E[Y_i | L_i , A_i = a] \right] \\
\end{aligned}
$$



In the first line, we use the law of iterated expectations. In the second line, we use the definition for counterfactual outcome $Y_i^{(a)}$ as specified in @eq-independence-swig. In the third line, we use the independence assumption (4) of the FFRCISTG. Fix $L_i = l$. Then $f_{Y}(U_{Y_i}, l, a) = Y_i^{(l, a)}$ and $A_i = A_i^{(l)}$, and (4) says that $L_i$, $A_i^{(l)}$ and $Y_i^{(l, a)}$ are mutually independent. Hence $f_{Y}(U_{Y_i} , L_i, a) \perp A_i | L_i$. In the fourth line we consider the expected value of $f_{Y}(U_{Y_i} , L_i, a)$ when $A_i = a$, in particular; positivity ensures this event has positive probability in every stratum of $L_i$. In the fifth line, we use the definition for observed value $Y_i$ as specified in @eq-independence-dag.
